F1: Each legacy-write goroutine derives its timeout context from the caller context, so caller cancellation can cancel the legacy write.
F2: Legacy errors are only recorded as metrics, and an unhandled panic in a goroutine can crash the process.
F3: Create and Update record storage failures as legacy duration, while DeleteCollection records a legacy call as storage duration.
F4: Delete passes the object name as the metric’s kind label, causing unbounded series cardinality.
F5: Delete returns on any storage error, including NotFound, without attempting the legacy delete.
F6: Legacy Update receives the raw objInfo rather than a wrapper containing the object returned by storage.
F7: The unconditional dry-run legacy writes predate this change, so the finding does not identify a newly changed behavior.
F8: This identifies test coverage and assertion weaknesses, not a behavior defect in the changed code.
